subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Data Collection from Minors
description: A short lesson to help you apply Data Collection from Minors.

hook.text: By the time a child turns 13, data brokers already have over 72 million data points about them.

buildup.text: Children's data comes from parents' posts, school platforms, gaming accounts, and family devices.

discovery.text: This data shapes what ads, content, and opportunities a child sees — before they can even understand data privacy.

twist.text: Children can't consent to data collection. But the data collected about them will follow them for life.

climax.text: A digital identity is built for every child before they're old enough to understand what privacy means.

punchline.text: Born into a profile. No consent possible.

quiz.question: Why is data collection from minors a unique privacy challenge?
options: Children can't meaningfully consent and the data follows them for life
Children's data is automatically deleted at age 18
No data is collected from children under current laws
